It features folk dance and music from across India, food fairs, handicraft stalls, water sports and cultural shows — the main cultural event of the season for visitors staying on Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island).

A week-long fair held around Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose's birth anniversary (January 23), organized by the administration in Port Blair. It combines cultural programs, exhibitions and local food stalls, and is one of the oldest community celebrations in the islands.

A beach carnival typically held in late April at Corbyn's Cove, Port Blair, celebrating the start of the summer season. It features beach games, water sports, food stalls, music and cultural performances — an easy add-on for Havelock visitors spending time in Port Blair.

A monsoon-season music and food festival held around July-August in the islands, with live music, local cuisine stalls and beach activities despite the rains. It gives monsoon travelers a reason to visit, though sea conditions limit inter-island water sports.

The Kerala harvest festival, celebrated by the large Malayali settler community across the Andaman Islands including Swaraj Dweep. Highlights include the traditional sadhya feast, pookalam flower carpets, and cultural programs in community halls and temples.

The festival of lights is celebrated across Swaraj Dweep and the Andaman Islands with lamps, fireworks and community gatherings, coinciding with the start of the peak tourist season. Shops and resorts decorate, and visitors can join the festive evenings in Govind Nagar village.

Held every year at Neil Island (Shaheed Dweep) in January to mark Swami Vivekananda's birth anniversary, with cultural programmes and local gatherings; one of the few festivals centred on Neil Island itself.

The Andaman & Nicobar Administration's flagship year-end festival; main venue at Sri Vijaya Puram with programmes staged on Shaheed Dweep too (live bands performed on the island during recent editions). Features cultural performances, food courts, handicraft stalls and children's activities.

Week-long patriotic festival on Swaraj Dweep (Havelock), about 17 km by ferry from Shaheed Dweep, held around Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose's birth anniversary; folk dances, patriotic songs, sports and exhibitions honouring the freedom movement.
Island-wide beach celebration promoting beach tourism, with beach volleyball, kabaddi, tug-of-war, local music and dance, sand-art competitions and island-style seafood stalls on the Andaman shores.

Music festival in Sri Vijaya Puram during the rainy months celebrating the islands' love of music, with live performances from local and mainland musicians across folk, classical, rock and fusion genres.
Tamil community festival celebrated across the Andaman & Nicobar Islands in honour of Lord Murugan, with processions of a decorated idol, hymns and drumming through island streets.
Marks the end of Ramadan. Celebrated by the whole island with prayers at the mosques followed by feasting on local delicacies; the most widely celebrated festival in Lakshadweep.
Festival of sacrifice marked by the sacrificial offering of a goat; observed with prayers and community feasting across the islands.
Celebrates the birth of Prophet Mohammad; islanders mark it with sweets, perfumes and community gatherings.

Lakshadweep's Island Festival celebrating the cultural heritage of the islands with traditional music, Kolkali stick dance and other folk dances, community gatherings, sports, boat races and displays of local arts and crafts.

The grandest celebration in Lakshadweep, marking the end of Ramadan. Islanders gather at mosques for special prayers, wear new clothes, prepare dishes like pathiri, biryani and halwa, and exchange sweets and gifts; Zakatul-Fitr charity is distributed to the needy.

The festival of sacrifice commemorating Prophet Ibrahim. Congregational prayers are followed by Qurbani, with meat shared among family, neighbours and the poor, emphasizing charity and community welfare.
The birth anniversary of Prophet Muhammad, observed with religious recitations, sermons and community prayers at decorated mosques, distribution of sweets, and charitable activities.

Solemn observance of Imam Hussain's martyrdom at Karbala, with special prayers, Majlis gatherings, Quran recitations and chest-beating taziya processions; many devotees distribute food and water (Sabeel) to the public.

Tamil Nadu's harvest festival celebrated over four days (Bhogi, Thai Pongal, Mattu Pongal, Kaanum Pongal), with the traditional sweet pongal dish cooked in new clay pots. Homes are decorated with kolams and sugarcane; cattle are honoured on Mattu Pongal.

Annual four-day festival organised by the Puducherry Department of Tourism since 1992/1993, drawing around a thousand delegates and yoga experts. Features yogasana competitions, discourses, workshops, lecture demonstrations, and cultural programmes, with the valedictory usually at Gandhi Thidal on Beach Road.

Annual temple festival on the full-moon day of the Tamil month of Masi, when temple deities are taken in procession to the sea for the theerthavari (holy dip). Celebrated grandly at Puducherry's seafront temples including the Manakula Vinayagar Temple.

Annual festival led by INTACH Puducherry, People for Pondicherry's Heritage, and PondyCAN with the Tourism Department, celebrating the city's built, natural, and living heritage. Programming includes heritage walks, open houses of historic buildings, craft bazaars, food walks, talks, and performances; the 9th edition ran 1 February–15 March.

France's National Day (14 July) celebrated with pride in the former French colony: wreath-laying at the French War Memorial on Beach Road by the District Collector and the French Consul General, with the police band playing the Indian and French anthems. French and Indian flags fly side by side across White Town.

The festival of lights celebrated across Puducherry with oil lamps, fireworks, and festive sweets; temples and White Town streets are illuminated. Dates follow the lunar calendar, usually falling in October or November.

The great mango festival of the Karaikal Ammaiyar Temple, celebrated on the full-moon day of the Tamil month of Aani. The deity's procession is showered with mangoes, and free mangoes and curd rice are distributed to devotees.

The district administration's annual tourism event (held Jan 16-18 in 2026) at the district stadium and Karaikal beach - a food festival, flower show, dog show, art and craft expo, cultural programmes and sports events.
The annual 10-day festival of the Mastan Syed Dawood Dargah - flag hoisting on a ship-mast-like pole, floats, music and fireworks, drawing devotees of the Sufi saint.
The 10-day feast of Our Lady of Angels Church - flag hoisting on Aug 6, feast on Aug 15. The image of the Virgin Mary is taken in a decorated chariot through Karaikal's streets.

The transit of Saturn from one zodiac sign to the next, observed every ~2.5 years at the Thirunallar Saniswaran Temple. Special poojas and abhishekams draw lakhs of devotees; expect very large crowds.

The 14-day death-anniversary (Urs) festival of Saint Syed Shahul Hameed at the Nagore Dargah - flag hoisting, Quran recitations, fireworks, and the famous sandalwood (santhanakoodu) procession. The 468th edition's flag hoisting was on 21 Nov 2025 per the dargah's official site.

festival_name: Feast of St. Teresa of Avila
description: The annual feast at St. Teresa's Shrine, Mahe's biggest religious festival, drawing thousands of devotees of all communities from across South India. The shrine is dedicated to St. Teresa of Avila, the town's patron.

Season of Theyyam ritual-art performances at kavus (sacred groves) around the Mahe-Thalassery region, including the famous Sri Muthappan Temple at Parassinikadavu. Night-long performances with elaborate costumes, fire rituals, and drumming.
Kerala's harvest festival, widely celebrated in Mahe with floral pookalams, traditional sadya feasts, and cultural programs, reflecting the town's Malayali roots.
The Malayali new year, observed in Mahe with the vishukkani ritual arrangement, fireworks, and festive meals.
Marks the de facto transfer of the French Indian territories, including Mahe, to India on 1 November 1954. Observed across the Union Territory with official ceremonies.

Yanam's most important annual festival: a 20-day Kalyanotsavam at the 15th-century Sri Rajarajeswara Temple (Sivalayam) in the month of Magha. Kalyanam is performed on Magha Shuddha Dvadashi; the deity is dressed as bridegroom and taken in chariot processions with Rathostavam and Trishulatirtham events.

Annual marriage festival (Kalyanotsavam) of Lord Venkanna Babu at Vishnalayam in the month of Phalguna. Commences on Phalguna Shuddha Padyami with the bridegroom-making of the Lord, followed by daily vahanam processions; Ponnavahanam, Ratha Yatra and Chakratirtham are the key events. Draws around 1.5 lakh devotees.

festival_name: Catholic Festival at St. Ann's Church
description: Annual Catholic festival at St. Ann's Church. Devotees, including Christians, Hindus and Muslims, come to honour and pray to Mother Mary.
10-day Brahmotsavam at Vishnalayam for Lord Venkanna Babu, conducted on the lines of the Tirupati Brahmotsavam, drawing large crowds.

Three-day annual cultural festival conducted by the Department of Art and Culture, Government of Puducherry, celebrating the territory's Franco-Tamil cultural fusion. Exact dates are announced each year; the August label is approximate.

Yanam People's Festival held in January. Historically linked to the Tuesday market (Marche du mardi / Mangalavaram Santa), when Telugu people from the Madras Presidency visited Yanam to buy foreign goods during the festival.
Ceremonial birthday parade in central London.
World-leading performing arts festival across Edinburgh.
Major cross-arts festival in Belfast.
Major Welsh-language cultural festival; location rotates.
